title: The Global Activation Status of a one-shot Primitive distinguishes acts that finish from acts that leave a persisting object
content:
All four of Obex's Genesis Primitives are one-shot, yet their Global Activation Statuses differ. Agent Creation is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.1.1), Prime Transformation is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.2.1.1), Executor Transformation is `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.3.1.1), and the Agent Token Primitive is `Active` (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.1.1).

The difference tracks whether the Invocation leaves behind something that still needs managing. Creation and transformation are events: once the Agent exists and is a Prime, the Primitive's Operational Process Definition can honestly say "no further operational process is needed post-deployment" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.2.3.1.2). Its Instance moves to Completed Instances.

The Agent Token Primitive is Invoked once but produces a durable object. Its Operational Process Definition is not empty — it covers "minting and initial distribution of the tokens from the Genesis Supply" — and its Instance stays under Active Instances. The Invocation is unrepeatable while the Instance remains live.

This separates two ideas that could easily be conflated: whether a Primitive can be Invoked again, and whether the resulting Instance is still operating. `Completed` describes an Instance with nothing left to do; the closure notice on In Progress Invocations describes a Primitive that can never be Invoked again. A single Primitive can be `Active` and permanently closed to new Invocations at the same time, and reading either status as implying the other will mislead.
description: Agent Creation and Prime Transformation read `Completed`, while the equally one-time Agent Token Primitive reads `Active` — because a deployed token remains under ongoing management.
